title: Inevitability of the Petz transpose map
authors: Jacopo Surace, Chenxu Li, Francesco Buscemi
abstract: Bayes' rule is central to classical statistical inference: given a prior and a stochastic model, it determines the corresponding retrodictive conditional probabilities. In quantum theory, however, the question of whether an equally general rule of retrodiction exists and, if so, whether it is uniquely determined remains nontrivial. Here we prove that a retrodiction assignment defined for all priors and channels, which takes each predicted output state back to its prior, must coincide with the Petz transpose map if it is involutive, respects sequential and parallel composition, and agrees with unitary inversion. The theorem holds for channels between finite-dimensional full matrix algebras, with the input and output spaces restricted to the supports of the corresponding reference states. In particular, affinity under probabilistic mixtures and the characteristic square-root dependence on the reference states follow from these requirements rather than being postulated. Without involutivity, the remaining requirements characterize a family of doubly rotated Petz maps. Our result thus explains why the Petz transpose map arises in seemingly different areas of quantum theory: it is the unique quantum analogue of Bayes' rule compatible with these consistency requirements.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that the Petz transpose map is the unique mathematical structure that serves as the quantum analogue of Bayes' rule. By imposing fundamental consistency requirements—such as composition rules and involutivity—on a general retrodiction assignment, the authors constrain the map to this specific, well-known form. This establishes the deep theoretical necessity of the Petz map across various areas of quantum physics.
main_problem: The paper seeks to find the unique quantum analogue of Bayes' rule (a retrodiction assignment) that is consistent with fundamental physical axioms in quantum theory.
main_result: The unique assignment satisfying the consistency requirements (involutivity, composition rules, unitary inversion) is proven to be the Petz transpose map, establishing its necessity.
method: The authors employ an axiomatic approach, imposing four consistency requirements on the retrodiction map and using algebraic constraints derived from composition rules to uniquely determine its functional form.
model_or_system: The theory applies to quantum channels acting on finite-dimensional full matrix algebras, characterized by input and output reference states ($\pi, \sigma$).
key_observables: The retrodiction assignment $R_{\pi 	o \sigma}[\Phi]$ and the Petz transpose map.
important_parameters: The reference states ($\pi, \sigma$), the channel $\Phi$, and the phase factor $t$ derived from continuity requirements.
main_assumptions: The theorem is proven for channels between finite-dimensional full matrix algebras, and the derivation relies heavily on assuming involutivity for the strongest result.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate controlled-swap circuits used to model the forward process and its retrodiction, linking the abstract axioms to concrete quantum circuit structures.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the retrodiction assignment based on classical analogy, then imposing four consistency axioms, and finally using these axioms—along with techniques involving ancillary systems and unitary conjugations—to derive the unique form of the Petz map.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep, axiomatic justification for the structure of quantum retrodiction, which is crucial for understanding measurement theory and state estimation in open quantum systems.
